summary: Verified live on 2026-08-14 by fetching primary sources (developers.figma.com, help.figma.com, forum.figma.com, GitHub raw files, npm/GitHub API). Headline findings for EXELMJ's ZIP + Markdown delivery: (1) Figma's official MCP server is now 23 primary tools + 6 Weave tools; `get_code` was renamed `get_design_context` and its output is NOT a design JSON at all — it is generated React+Tailwind source with `data-node-id`/`data-name` attributes plus imperative English instructions embedded in the tool result ("SUPER CRITICAL…", "you MUST call get_screenshot"). That means Figma's real "format" is code-as-interchange, which is lossy and un-diffable. (2) The only structured surfaces are `get_metadata` (sparse XML: id, name, type, x/y/w/h — no styling) and `get_variable_defs` (flat name→value with resolvedType, collection, scopes, codeSyntax). (3) Assets are served out-of-band from a localhost HTTP server (`http://127.0.0.1:3845/assets/<sha1>.png|.svg`) with three configurable modes: placeholder / local server / download-into-project. (4) The field-tested Dev Mode inspect list (box model, layout+spacing, typography, text strings, colours, component properties, styles+variables shown as token-name AND resolved value side by side, prototype interactions, Assets, Export settings, Code Connect snippet) is still the best checklist of "what a human needs to build this". (5) The best OSS intermediate JSON is Framelink `figma-developer-mcp` v0.13.2 (MIT): `SimplifiedDesign{name, nodes, components, componentSets, globalVars, elements}` with a genuinely clever two-level dedup (styles hoisted to `globalVars` only at 2+ references or if named; whole node bodies hashed and hoisted to `elements` with a `template` reference) — copy this wholesale. (6) The documented FAILURES are where EXELMJ's format earns its place: variable ALIASES are flattened to final values, only the DEFAULT MODE is returned (Figma confirmed multi-mode is "on our list", May 2026), component VARIANTS return the base component's tokens not the variant's, generated code often emits raw hex with no token reference at all, responses blow past context limits (a real error: "response (351378 tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)"), and there is zero support for text direction/RTL, zero captured-from-web provenance, and no per-node geometry fallback when auto-layout is absent. CAUTION: bernaferrari/FigmaToCode is GPL-3.0 — reference-only, must be labelled; everything else recommended here is MIT or MPL-2.0.

formats.name: Figma MCP server — get_design_context (formerly get_code)
formats.what_it_is: The primary design-to-code tool of Figma's official MCP server. Takes a nodeId (or the desktop app's current selection) and returns generated UI source code, not a data model. Default output is React + Tailwind; the target framework is steered by prompt/rules rather than by a parameter.
formats.current_version_status: Live and current as of 2026-08-14. The docs page 'Tools and prompts' fetched today lists 23 primary tools plus 6 Weave tools. `get_code` was renamed `get_design_context` (rename already in effect by 2025-10-17 per forum threads); older blog posts and some third-party MCP catalogues still say `get_code`. Desktop server at http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp, remote at https://mcp.figma.com/mcp; selection-based input is desktop-only, remote is link-only. Assets/write features and several tools are still labelled beta/free-during-beta.
formats.structure: Output = a code string (JSX/Tailwind by default) carrying: className attributes; `data-node-id` and `data-name` attributes tying each element back to the Figma node; image/SVG references as absolute localhost URLs (e.g. const img = "http://localhost:3845/assets/0f46fbf7be0964a515990e4283d4dc25d73db9bb.svg"). Three asset modes are configurable: Placeholder (generic filenames), Local Server (http://127.0.0.1:3845/assets/{hash}), Download (real file paths written into the project). Crucially the payload also contains natural-language directives aimed at the agent, e.g. "SUPER CRITICAL: The generated React+Tailwind code MUST be converted to match the target project's technology stack and styling system" and "IMPORTANT: After you call this tool, you MUST call get_screenshot", plus "If the Figma MCP server returns a localhost source for an image or SVG, use that source directly, and do NOT use or create placeholders". Auto Layout is not emitted as data — it is baked into flex/grid Tailwind classes. Component instances are only resolved to real code components when a Code Connect mapping exists.
formats.worth_copying: Two ideas only: (a) the `data-node-id` back-reference on every emitted element, which makes generated code re-syncable and diffable against the source — EXELMJ should stamp `data-exelmj-id` on every node it emits in the Markdown/ZIP; (b) the explicit, machine-readable asset-mode switch (placeholder | server URL | on-disk path) so the consumer knows exactly how to resolve an image reference. Do NOT copy the code-as-interchange decision: shipping React+Tailwind forces every consumer through a lossy re-interpretation and destroys the token layer (see the documented hex-only complaint). And do NOT copy the embedding of imperative instructions inside the data payload — dev.to's teardown correctly flags MCP tool responses as a prompt-injection surface; EXELMJ should keep instructions in a separate, clearly-fenced 'how to read this' section of the Markdown, never interleaved with node data.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma product; requires Dev or Full seat for the desktop server). Reference-only — do not copy code, only shape ideas.

formats.name: Figma MCP server — get_metadata (sparse XML index)
formats.what_it_is: A deliberately cheap 'map of the file' tool. Exists purely because get_design_context routinely overflows the agent's context window. When called with no nodeId it lists the file's top-level pages.
formats.current_version_status: Live as of 2026-08-14. Figma's own recommended flow (mcp-server-guide README, fetched today) is: call get_design_context first; if the response is too large or truncated, call get_metadata to get the high-level node map, then re-fetch only the required node(s). Real failure that motivates it, reported by users: "Error: MCP tool 'get_design_context' response (351378 tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)" (Claude Code's default 25k MCP response cap). There are open 2026 forum reports that get_metadata sometimes returns instruction text only.
formats.structure: XML, not JSON. A sparse tree where each element carries only: layer id, name, type, position (x, y) and size (width, height). Explicitly NO styling, no fills, no typography, no children content — 'only for getting an overview of the structure'. Nested to mirror the layer tree.
formats.worth_copying: The two-tier progressive-disclosure pattern is the single most important structural lesson for EXELMJ's Markdown deliverable: ship a cheap flat INDEX (id, name, type, artboard, w/h, one-line role) at the top of the Markdown and in the ZIP as its own small file, then the full per-node detail below/in separate files. An agent can then read the index, decide which artboard it needs, and jump. Also copy the choice of a tag-tree (XML/heading-tree) for the index — it survives truncation far better than a giant JSON object, because a truncated JSON is unparseable while a truncated heading tree is still 80% useful. For the Markdown file specifically, the index should be a Markdown table (grep-able, line-oriented) rather than XML.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma). Shape idea only.

formats.name: Figma MCP server — get_variable_defs (token extraction)
formats.what_it_is: Returns the design variables and styles actually used by the current selection — colours, spacing, typography — so the model references token names instead of hardcoding hex. Desktop-only; not available on the remote server at mcp.figma.com.
formats.current_version_status: Live as of 2026-08-14 but with THREE confirmed, unfixed defects documented on Figma's own forum. (1) Aliases are flattened: 'get_variable_defs seems to return the final resolved value and not the alias in some cases' (forum 47630) — so semantic→primitive token chains are destroyed. (2) Only the default mode is returned; a Figma staff member (Yarden K) confirmed multi-mode reading 'is definitely in our list' with no timeline, latest activity May 2026 (forum 42031). (3) Variant mismatch: for a non-base variant, get_variable_defs returns the variant's real tokens (e.g. surface/neutral/primary-hover) while get_design_context returns the BASE component's tokens (surface/neutral/primary) — 'impossible to programmatically audit or generate accurate code for component variants' (forum 50790).
formats.structure: A flat name→value map per selection. Per-variable fields documented: variable name (semantic identifier), value (variable.valuesByMode[modeId] resolved for the current mode only), type (variable.resolvedType), collection (variable.variableCollectionId), scopes (variable.scopes — e.g. ["GAP"], ["TEXT_FILL"], ["WIDTH_HEIGHT"], ["FONT_FAMILY"]), and codeSyntax (platform-specific strings such as "var(--color-bg-default)"). Separately, a completely different complaint (forum 42174) is that get_code's own output 'outputs Tailwind classes without any reference to Figma variables' — raw #ffffff, forcing the agent to guess the token.
formats.worth_copying: COPY: `scopes` and `codeSyntax`. Scopes are the field almost nobody else has and they are what stops an agent using a gap token as a text colour — EXELMJ's token entries should carry an explicit usage scope list. codeSyntax (the exact CSS custom-property / platform string to emit) removes an entire class of naming guesswork. DO THE OPPOSITE of the rest: EXELMJ must emit BOTH the unresolved alias chain (token → token → primitive) AND the resolved literal, must emit ALL modes (light/dark, ar/en, density) not just the default, and must bind tokens per component STATE/variant rather than to the base definition. Those three inversions are directly justified by three live Figma bug reports and are the clearest place our format beats the incumbent.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma). Field names are documentation facts, not copyrightable structure — safe to be inspired by.

formats.name: Figma MCP server — get_screenshot
formats.what_it_is: Renders the selected node to an image and returns it inline so the agent can visually verify layout fidelity. Figma's own get_design_context response instructs the agent to call it immediately afterwards.
formats.current_version_status: Live as of 2026-08-14. Returns a PNG, supported inline as base64 in the MCP tool result. Known live bug: the server declares the media type as image/jpeg while the bytes are actually PNG, which triggers an API error in some clients (multiple 2026 forum reports, e.g. thread 47545).
formats.structure: An MCP image content block: base64-encoded PNG plus a declared mime type. No coordinates, no overlay, no mapping back to node ids — it is a flat picture of one selection.
formats.worth_copying: COPY the principle: ship a rendered ground-truth raster of every artboard alongside the structured data. Builder.io's critique of the Figma MCP names the absence of rendered feedback as one of three fundamental limitations — 'no visibility into the final, rendered output of its own code'. For EXELMJ: the ZIP must contain `previews/<artboard-id>.png` for every artboard (and ideally per component and per state), and the Markdown must reference them by relative path. IMPROVE on it in two ways Figma doesn't: (a) declare the mime type correctly and state the pixel dimensions and device-pixel-ratio next to the reference (Figma's own mime bug is the cautionary tale); (b) because a single Markdown file cannot carry a PNG cheaply, use small inline data: URIs only for icons/thumbnails and otherwise reference the ZIP-relative path, with an explicit note that the Markdown-only delivery is preview-less by design.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma).

formats.name: Figma MCP server — get_code_connect_map, download_assets, get_motion_context
formats.what_it_is: The three supporting tools that carry the information the main code tool cannot: which existing code component a design node corresponds to, how to get the real asset bytes, and how a node animates.
formats.current_version_status: All live as of 2026-08-14 per the tools-and-prompts page fetched today. download_assets and several siblings are remote-only. get_motion_context is a comparatively recent addition and is the only motion surface.
formats.structure: get_code_connect_map returns a flat object keyed by Figma node id: {'1:2': { codeConnectSrc: 'https://github.com/foo/components/Button.tsx', codeConnectName: 'Button' }} — codeConnectSrc is the file location (URL or repo-relative path), codeConnectName the exported component name; richer variants also return name, source, snippet data, version and framework label. download_assets returns TEMPORARY URLs, max 20 nodes per call, formats PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF, and has a raw mode that returns 'the original uploaded source files (the exact JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP placed as a fill) without re-rendering'. get_motion_context returns keyframe animation data for animated nodes as CSS @keyframes plus motion.dev code snippets, with `recursive: true` to include all descendants. get_context_for_code_connect returns property definitions, variants, and a descendant tree.
formats.worth_copying: COPY three things. (1) The node-id-keyed mapping table as a first-class top-level section — EXELMJ should have a `bindings` map from captured/design node id → target code symbol, because Figma's own guidance is that without Code Connect the generated styling is 85–90% inaccurate. (2) download_assets' RAW mode distinction — original uploaded bytes vs re-rendered export are different things and the format must say which one it is shipping; EXELMJ's ZIP should carry both `assets/original/` and `assets/rendered/` where they differ, with the intrinsic natural width/height recorded (EXELMJ's PlacedImage already has naturalW/naturalH — keep it). (3) get_motion_context's dual emission: keyframes as BOTH raw CSS @keyframes AND a library-flavoured snippet. EXELMJ captures motion keyframes from live sites already; emit them as literal CSS @keyframes plus the trigger/state that fires them, never as prose. AVOID download_assets' temporary URLs and 20-node batch cap — an offline ZIP has no such excuse and should embed every byte.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma). Note @figma/code-connect itself, the client tooling, is MIT.

formats.name: Figma Dev Mode inspect / spec panel (the human handoff checklist)
formats.what_it_is: The pre-MCP, decade-field-tested answer to 'what does a person need in order to build this screen'. Worth treating as the required-field checklist for EXELMJ's Markdown, because every item on it survived years of real developer use.
formats.current_version_status: Current as of 2026-08-14; both help.figma.com articles fetched today (Guide to inspecting; Inspect designs in Dev Mode). Dev Mode now requires a Dev or Full seat. The Properties tab in Design mode and the Inspect tab in Dev Mode expose the same core list.
formats.structure: Panel sections, verbatim from Figma's docs: the selected layer's NAME and TYPE (component, instance, frame, text…) at the top; a CODE section that shows a typographic preview for text selections and a BOX MODEL (margin, border, padding) for everything else, followed by layout and style info, with selectable language and units; the property list — 'layout, color, typography, text strings, component properties, styles, and variables'; applied STYLES AND VARIABLES shown as token name AND resolved value side by side (e.g. color/primary/500 – #3B82F6); PROTOTYPE INTERACTIONS; component metadata (keywords, layout, variant information, component properties) and a component PLAYGROUND for trying properties and variable modes; CODE CONNECT snippets replacing autogenerated code; an ASSETS section auto-detecting downloadable icons plus GIFs, MP4s and full-resolution source files; an EXPORT section with PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF settings; change history/diff against the previous version or the main component; and links out to GitHub, Jira, Storybook, VS Code.
formats.worth_copying: Treat this as the mandatory field list for every node section in EXELMJ's Markdown: name+type, box model (padding/border/margin), layout+spacing, typography, literal text strings, colours, component properties, styles+variables shown as token-name AND resolved-value together, interactions, assets, export settings. Two items deserve special emphasis because agents fail without them and no JSON format above carries them well: (a) the side-by-side token-name AND resolved-value presentation — never one or the other; (b) the DIFF-against-main-component idea, i.e. for every component instance record only its OVERRIDES relative to the definition, which is both smaller and semantically correct. The 'typographic preview vs box model' split is also a good Markdown pattern: text nodes and box nodes should render with different templates rather than one generic property dump.
formats.license: Proprietary (Figma product UI). Checklist of concepts only.

formats.name: Framelink figma-developer-mcp — SimplifiedDesign JSON (best OSS intermediate)
formats.what_it_is: An open-source MCP server that hits the Figma REST API and hands the agent a heavily-compressed, agent-shaped JSON instead of raw Figma nodes. Its README claims ~90% compression versus the raw API response. This is the closest existing thing to what EXELMJ needs to emit, and it is permissively licensed.
formats.current_version_status: npm package `figma-developer-mcp` v0.13.2, MIT, verified from package.json on main 2026-08-14. Actively maintained; source tree at src/{extractors,transformers,services}. Exposes `get_figma_data` (layout & styling JSON) and `download_figma_images`.
formats.structure: Verbatim from src/extractors/types.ts: `interface SimplifiedDesign { name: string; nodes: SimplifiedNode[]; components: Record<string, SimplifiedComponentDefinition>; componentSets: Record<string, SimplifiedComponentSetDefinition>; globalVars: GlobalVars; elements: Record<string, ElementBody>; }` where `GlobalVars = { styles: Record<string, StyleTypes> }` and `ElementBody = Omit<SimplifiedNode,'id'|'name'|'children'|'template'>`. SimplifiedNode: id, name?, type?, template?, text?, textStyle?, boldWeight?, fills?, styles?, strokes?, strokeWeight?, strokeDashes?, strokeWeights?, strokeAlign? ('INSIDE'|'OUTSIDE'|'CENTER'), effects?, opacity?, borderRadius?, layout?, componentId?, componentProperties?: Record<string, boolean|string>, componentPropertyReferences?, children?. Note every style-ish field is `string | RealObject` — the string is a key into globalVars.styles. SimplifiedLayout (src/transformers/layout/common.ts, verbatim): mode: 'none'|'row'|'column'|'grid'; justifyContent?; alignItems?; alignSelf?; wrap?: boolean; gap?: string; gridTemplateColumns?; gridTemplateRows?; gridColumn?; gridRow?; justifySelf?; zIndex?: number; locationRelativeToParent?: {x,y}; dimensions?: {width?, height?, aspectRatio?}; designedWidth?: string; designedHeight?: string; padding?: string; sizing?: {horizontal?: 'fixed'|'fill'|'hug'|'contextual', vertical?: same}; overflowScroll?: ('x'|'y')[]; position?: 'absolute'. Components: SimplifiedComponentDefinition{id, key, name, componentSetId?, propertyDefinitions?: Record<string, {type: string; defaultValue: boolean|string}>}; SimplifiedComponentSetDefinition adds description.
formats.worth_copying: This is the single most copyable artefact in the whole survey, for four specific things. (1) THE STRING-OR-OBJECT UNION: `fills?: string | SimplifiedFill[]` — a shared style is a short key into a global table, a one-off style is inlined at the node. (2) THE COUNT-GATE HOISTING RULE from src/extractors/finalize.ts, verbatim: 'a style stays in globalVars only when 2+ nodes reference it (or it's a named Figma style)'; single-use styles are inlined to kill pointer-chasing, named styles are kept regardless to preserve design-system intent, and orphan named styles with zero references are dropped as noise. (3) ELEMENT-BODY DEDUP: node bodies (everything except id/name/children) that appear 2+ times are hashed (truncated SHA-1, lengthened on collision) and emitted once into `elements`, each occurrence collapsing to `{ id, name, template, children? }`. (4) SimplifiedLayout's `sizing: {horizontal, vertical} ∈ fixed|fill|hug|contextual` plus `designedWidth/designedHeight` alongside `dimensions` — this is exactly the fixed-vs-fluid distinction EXELMJ's auto-layout frames need, and `position:'absolute'` + `locationRelativeToParent` is the correct escape hatch for free-positioned artboard content, which maps cleanly onto EXELMJ's existing PDF-point x/y/w/h shapes. Its WEAKNESS to fix: everything is CSS-flavoured strings ('padding' as one string, 'gap' as a string), which is lossy and locale-blind; and there is no state/variant, no motion, no direction/RTL, and no asset bytes in the JSON at all.
formats.license: MIT — usable, including copying the type shapes.

formats.name: Figma Code Connect (mapping format)
formats.what_it_is: Figma's official, permissively-licensed toolkit for declaring 'this Figma component IS this code component, and these design properties map to these props'. The declaration lives in the codebase as .figma.ts files.
formats.current_version_status: MIT, 1,557 stars, last push 2026-08-12 (GitHub API, checked 2026-08-14). Actively developed. The newer 'parserless' style is now the one Figma's own skill recommends: create .figma.ts (not .figma.tsx) files using figma.code`...` tagged templates, and do NOT use the parser-based figma.connect().
formats.structure: Two generations. Parser-based (older, still widely documented): figma.connect(Button, '<FIGMA_URL>', { props: { variant: figma.enum('Variant', { Primary: 'primary' }), children: figma.string('Label') } }). Parserless: figma.code`...` tagged templates with typed property accessors — getString() for TEXT, getBoolean() for BOOLEAN (with optional mapped values), getEnum() with EXHAUSTIVE value mappings for VARIANT, getInstanceSwap() for swappable nested instances, getSlot() only for SLOT-type properties, findInstance()/findConnectedInstance() for unnamed child layers. Hard rules from the official skill: never string-concatenate template results (always interpolate), check type==='INSTANCE' before executeTemplate(), wrap strings in quotes and instance values in braces, handle every variant value exhaustively to prevent undefined output, never hardcode children or invent props.
formats.worth_copying: COPY the property-type taxonomy — TEXT / BOOLEAN / VARIANT(enum) / INSTANCE_SWAP / SLOT is a small, complete, battle-tested vocabulary for component props, and EXELMJ's component/template system should use exactly these five kinds rather than inventing its own. COPY the exhaustiveness rule: every enum/variant value must have an explicit mapping, because a missing case silently produces undefined output — in a Markdown deliverable that means every component section must list ALL its variant values in a table with no 'etc.'. COPY the slot concept for children/composition. The mapping table itself belongs in EXELMJ's ZIP as a standalone `bindings.json`/`bindings.md` so it can be edited by hand without touching the design data.
formats.license: MIT.

formats.name: @figma/rest-api-spec — canonical node typings
formats.what_it_is: Figma's own TypeScript typings for the REST API node graph. This is the ground-truth vocabulary that every design-to-code tool (including Framelink, which imports it directly) is a lossy projection of.
formats.current_version_status: v0.42.0, MIT (verified from package.json on main, 2026-08-14). Description verbatim: 'Typings for the Figma REST API'.
formats.structure: Full Figma document model: Node union (FRAME, GROUP, TEXT, RECTANGLE, VECTOR, COMPONENT, COMPONENT_SET, INSTANCE, …), Paint/fills, Effect, LayoutConstraint, absoluteBoundingBox, TypeStyle, Style, ExportSetting, plus component and componentSet dictionaries at the file level. Framelink imports `Node as FigmaDocumentNode` and `Style` straight from it.
formats.worth_copying: Use it as the CHECKLIST of what a complete visual node model contains, not as a shape to copy — it is far too verbose for an agent payload (hence Framelink's 90% compression). Two specifics worth lifting: the separation of `absoluteBoundingBox` from layout-relative position (EXELMJ needs both, since captured web components have only overall w/h and no per-node geometry), and the file-level `components`/`componentSets` dictionaries being siblings of the node tree rather than nested inside it — definition-once, reference-many.
formats.license: MIT.

formats.name: Builder.io Figma import — figma-to-builder JSON + 'Precise Mode' rules
formats.what_it_is: Builder's design-import path: the Figma plugin serialises the selection and POSTs it to a conversion API which returns Builder content JSON (their block format), which then drives code generation. Their published import rules are the most honest public statement of what a design-to-code converter cannot infer.
formats.current_version_status: Live as of 2026-08-14. The conversion endpoint is builder.io/api/v1/figma-to-builder, documented in BuilderIO/figma-html DEVELOP.md as converting 'a Figma design to a Builder content JSON'; the plugin has a 'Download JSON' button that dumps the serialised Figma input for offline iteration. The Builder content JSON block schema itself is NOT publicly documented in the repo — I could not verify the exact block field names from a primary source, so treat any @builder.io/sdk:Element field list as unverified. The related @builder.io/html-to-figma package is MIT (package.json checked today), version 0.0.5-3.
formats.structure: Pipeline shape: [serialised Figma JSON] → POST /api/v1/figma-to-builder → [Builder content JSON of nested blocks with styles and responsive styles]. The load-bearing public content is the Precise Mode requirement list, verbatim: 'Always apply Auto Layout to your Figma file' — 'Converting your design to use Auto Layout is the best way to ensure it imports well'; 'Always explicitly define images' (select the element and expand the Export section so the AI identifies it as an image with certainty); 'Minimize overlapping and intersections between elements, as intersections can lead to undesirable results'; 'Excessive space in the bounding box can lead to issues in the output, including extra whitespace and line breaks within text layers'; 'Transparency effects, such as translucency or opacity, can pose challenges in the interpretation of the design'.
formats.worth_copying: COPY the diagnosis, not the format. Builder's rule list is a confession that absolute pixel positions cannot be reliably inverted into layout intent, that an importer cannot tell a decorative raster from a group of vectors, and that loose text bounding boxes produce phantom whitespace. EXELMJ has a structural advantage here and should exploit it: its authoring tool OWNS the auto-layout frames, so it should emit layout intent directly (never make the consumer re-infer it), emit an explicit `role: image | icon | text | container` per node (never make the consumer guess), and emit text nodes with the measured text metrics rather than the box. The 'Download JSON' fixture idea is also worth copying operationally: EXELMJ's ZIP should be a self-contained fixture that can be replayed into the converter for regression tests.
formats.license: Builder platform is proprietary; @builder.io/html-to-figma is MIT. The block schema is unverified — do not cite field names without checking the SDK.

formats.name: bernaferrari/FigmaToCode — AltNodes intermediate representation
formats.what_it_is: The best-known OSS Figma-to-code plugin. Its interesting contribution is architectural: it does not walk Figma's nodes directly, it builds a virtualised parallel tree called AltNodes and optimises the LAYOUT on that tree before any code is emitted.
formats.current_version_status: GPL-3.0, 5,124 stars, last push 2026-08-05 (GitHub API, checked 2026-08-14). Targets HTML, Tailwind, Flutter and SwiftUI, with Jetpack Compose, React Native, Bootstrap and Fluent UI listed as planned.
formats.structure: Figma nodes → AltNodes (a remade, mutable copy of the official node implementation, so the user's real file is never altered) → layout optimisation and analysis pass → target-language emitter. README notes a concrete emitter constraint worth knowing: Tailwind's max width is 384px, so larger elements fall back to w-full unless relative widths like w-1/2 are used.
formats.worth_copying: COPY THE ARCHITECTURE IDEA ONLY, AND LABEL IT: this project is GPL-3.0, therefore REFERENCE-ONLY under EXELMJ's permissive-licence constraint — no code, no type definitions, no file may be lifted. The idea worth taking is the separate normalisation pass: don't serialise the editor's live model straight to the deliverable; build a normalised intermediate first (resolve auto-layout, collapse redundant wrapper groups, decide fixed-vs-fluid, promote repeated subtrees to components), then serialise that. It also demonstrates the multi-target argument for staying framework-neutral in the payload: the same IR feeds Tailwind, Flutter and SwiftUI, which is impossible if your interchange format is React source — a direct rebuttal of Figma's get_design_context design.
formats.license: GPL-3.0 — REFERENCE-ONLY, must be labelled as such. Do not copy code or type shapes into EXELMJ.

formats.name: Penpot .penpot v3 — a real ZIP design-file format
formats.what_it_is: The closest existing prior art to EXELMJ's ZIP deliverable specifically: an open, permissively-licensed, ZIP-plus-JSON design file format from a shipping design tool, with a published spec.
formats.current_version_status: Penpot repo is MPL-2.0, last push 2026-08-13 (GitHub API, checked 2026-08-14). Format version v3 = ZIP + JSON is current; v1 (binary) is deprecated but still importable. Penpot exports two flavours: the binary/efficient .penpot and a standard .zip of SVG + JSON intended to be readable by other software. Penpot natively supports the Design Tokens Community Group JSON format, and the separate penpot-export devtool emits tokens as CSS/SCSS/JSON per the DTCG second editor's draft.
formats.structure: Verbatim layout: your-design.penpot (ZIP archive) ├── manifest.json ├── files/ │ ├── file-metadata.json │ └── file-data/ │ ├── pages/ │ ├── colors/ │ ├── components/ │ ├── typographies/ │ ├── tokens.json │ └── media/ └── objects/. manifest.json is 'the table of contents' recording which format version is used and which Penpot version created the file. objects/ holds 'the actual binary files (PNG, JPG, SVG) referenced by your design. Each object has a JSON metadata file alongside the binary file.' Files carry a format version and feature flags indicating which capabilities were used.
formats.worth_copying: COPY THIS DIRECTORY SHAPE almost verbatim for EXELMJ's ZIP — it is the validated answer. Specifically: (1) a top-level manifest.json carrying format version + producing-app version + FEATURE FLAGS declaring which capabilities the file uses, so a future consumer can fail loudly instead of silently mis-rendering (EXELMJ's DesignProject already has version and source — promote them into a real manifest); (2) one directory per concern (pages, colors, components, typographies, tokens, media) rather than one giant document, which makes the ZIP diffable in git and lets an agent read only what it needs; (3) tokens.json as its own file in DTCG format rather than a bespoke token blob — this buys interop with Style Dictionary and every token pipeline for free; (4) binary assets in their own directory with a JSON SIDECAR per object carrying its metadata (mime, natural dimensions, origin URL for web-captured assets, licence) — EXELMJ's PlacedImage dataURL should become a real file plus sidecar in the ZIP, and stay a data: URI only in the single-Markdown delivery. (5) The dual-export idea (efficient native format vs a standard interchange zip) is a good precedent for EXELMJ shipping ZIP and Markdown as siblings from one model.
formats.license: MPL-2.0 (Penpot core). MPL-2.0 is on EXELMJ's allowed list; the format documentation is freely usable.

formats.name: Anima / Locofy — negative result, no public intermediate format
formats.what_it_is: The two best-known commercial Figma-to-code products. I searched for a published intermediate representation for both and found none — this is a reportable negative result, not an omission.
formats.current_version_status: Both live and commercially active as of 2026 per multiple 2026 comparison articles fetched today. Anima exports design systems as React, HTML/CSS or Tailwind and is generally judged better for design QA and interactive prototypes than for production code generation. Locofy generates React, Next.js, Vue, Angular and Gatsby and works by having the designer TAG components inside Figma before export, which guides the generator. Neither publishes a schema, an IR, or an open export format; both are closed SaaS pipelines.
formats.structure: No public schema for either. The only architecturally interesting, publicly-visible mechanism is Locofy's in-design tagging: the human annotates which layers are buttons, inputs, lists, links and repeatable items BEFORE generation, supplying the semantic layer that geometry alone cannot provide.
formats.worth_copying: COPY LOCOFY'S TAGGING INSIGHT, which is the whole lesson from this pair: the semantics an agent needs (this is a button, this is a list that repeats, this is an input, this row is a template) cannot be derived from geometry and styling and must be AUTHORED. EXELMJ's studio should let the designer tag semantic role, interactive state set, and repeat-ability on any node, and the ZIP/Markdown must carry those tags as first-class fields. That is cheap for EXELMJ (it owns the authoring UI) and is precisely what Figma's MCP cannot supply. Also note for expectation-setting: the fact that two funded companies keep their IR closed means there is no incumbent open standard for this payload — EXELMJ's format has genuinely open ground to occupy.
formats.license: Proprietary/closed SaaS. Nothing copyable beyond the tagging concept.

llm_needs.need: A stable, source-traceable id on every node, echoed into whatever the agent emits
llm_needs.why: Figma's own get_design_context stamps `data-node-id` and `data-name` onto every generated element. That is the only reason generated code can later be diffed, re-synced, or audited against the design.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent produces a one-shot dump. On the second delivery nothing can be matched to anything: the human cannot ask 'why did the login button change', the agent cannot do an incremental update, and every re-generation is a full rewrite that discards hand edits. This is exactly the 'each design-to-code roundtrip is lossy' failure ByteByteGo describes.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Every node in the ZIP JSON and every section heading in the Markdown carries a short stable id (e.g. `art-01/frame-03/btn-primary`). Markdown headings become `### btn-primary — Primary button {#exelmj:art-01.frame-03.btn-primary}`. Instruct consumers to emit `data-exelmj-id` on the produced element. Ids must be derived from the design model and survive renames.

llm_needs.need: Layout intent as structured fields — direction, gap, padding, alignment, and per-axis sizing (fixed | fill | hug) — never as reconstructed pixel positions
llm_needs.why: Framelink's SimplifiedLayout carries exactly this: mode row|column|grid, gap, padding, justifyContent, alignItems, alignSelf, wrap, sizing{horizontal, vertical} ∈ fixed|fill|hug|contextual, plus designedWidth/designedHeight and an escape hatch of position:'absolute' with locationRelativeToParent. Builder.io's Precise Mode docs demand 'Always apply Auto Layout to your Figma file' because the converter cannot invert absolute coordinates back into intent.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent hardcodes the design-time pixel width as a literal. The result looks right at exactly one viewport and breaks everywhere else: a 'fill' button becomes 327px wide, a 'hug' chip gets a fixed width and clips its label in Arabic, and adding one list item overflows the container. Nothing in the output tells the agent which numbers were intentional and which were incidental.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Emit an explicit layout object per container: {mode, gap, padding{t,r,b,l}, justify, align, wrap} and per child {sizing:{h,v}, alignSelf, designedW, designedH, minW/maxW}. Mark every dimension as either INTENT (a constraint the developer must honour) or MEASURED (an incidental design-time value) — one boolean per number is enough and it is the highest-value field in the whole format. For EXELMJ's free-positioned artboard shapes, fall back to position:'absolute' + x/y in the artboard's units and say so explicitly rather than pretending it is flow layout.

llm_needs.need: Tokens with the alias chain AND the resolved value AND every mode — plus a usage scope
llm_needs.why: Three separate live Figma bug reports establish the failure: get_variable_defs 'seems to return the final resolved value and not the alias in some cases' (forum 47630, closed with no reply); it returns only the default mode, with Figma staff confirming multi-mode is merely 'in our list' as of May 2026 (forum 42031); and get_code 'outputs Tailwind classes without any reference to Figma variables' — raw #ffffff only (forum 42174). Conversely the fields Figma does get right, `scopes` (e.g. ["GAP"], ["TEXT_FILL"]) and `codeSyntax` (e.g. "var(--color-bg-default)"), are the ones that prevent misuse.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent hardcodes hex. Dark mode, high contrast and Arabic-vs-Latin typography variants become impossible without re-deriving the whole theme by hand; two semantically different tokens that happen to share a hex value get collapsed into one; and a spacing token gets used as a text colour because nothing said it couldn't. The design system is silently destroyed at the moment of handoff — the exact complaint that the tool is only 'a basic vibe coding tool'.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: A tokens section in DTCG JSON (Penpot's precedent — it ships tokens.json natively in DTCG format, and penpot-export targets the DTCG second editor's draft) with, per token: name, $type, per-mode values keyed by mode id, the alias reference preserved as a reference (`{color.brand.500}`) not flattened, the resolved literal for each mode as a convenience field clearly marked as derived, a `scopes` array, and a `codeSyntax` string per platform. In the Markdown, one table per collection with columns Token | Type | Scope | Value (light) | Value (dark) | Alias of | CSS var. Every node property that uses a token must reference the token NAME, with the literal in parentheses — the Dev Mode 'color/primary/500 – #3B82F6' side-by-side pattern.

llm_needs.need: Component definition and instance split, with instances carrying only their overrides and their variant-correct token bindings
llm_needs.why: Framelink models this as file-level `components` and `componentSets` dictionaries (SimplifiedComponentDefinition{id, key, name, componentSetId?, propertyDefinitions:{type, defaultValue}}) sitting beside the node tree, with nodes referencing componentId + componentProperties. Figma's Dev Mode shows an instance diffed against its main component. And Figma's live variant bug (forum 50790) proves the cost of getting the binding wrong: get_design_context returns the BASE component's tokens for a non-base variant, making it 'impossible to programmatically audit or generate accurate code for component variants'.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent writes fifty near-identical button implementations, one per usage site — Michel Velis's exact description of a Code-Connect-less workflow. Worse, the hover/disabled variants all get the resting state's colours, so the built UI has no visible state changes and the bug is invisible in review because the resting screenshot matches.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Top-level `components` map: id → {name, props:[{name, kind: text|boolean|variant|instanceSwap|slot, values[], default}], states, tokensByState}. Nodes carry {componentId, props:{...}} and ONLY the overrides that differ from the definition. Bind tokens per state/variant, never once at the definition. Use Code Connect's five-kind prop taxonomy verbatim and list every variant value exhaustively — the official skill's rule is that a missing enum case yields undefined output.

llm_needs.need: Interactive states and motion as literal declarative data (state → property deltas; keyframes as CSS @keyframes plus trigger)
llm_needs.why: EXELMJ's element picker already captures states and motion keyframes, and Figma's get_motion_context proves the useful emission shape: keyframe data rendered as CSS @keyframes AND a library snippet (motion.dev), with `recursive:true` to include descendants. Dev Mode's inspect panel likewise lists prototype interactions as a first-class section.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: States get described in prose ('the button darkens on hover') and the agent invents a plausible-but-wrong value, or omits :focus-visible entirely, or writes a 150ms ease when the captured original was a 220ms cubic-bezier spring. The rebuilt UI feels wrong in a way no static screenshot comparison catches.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Per component: a `states` map (default, hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, loading, selected, error) where each entry is a DELTA of changed properties only, plus `motion`: {trigger, duration, easing, delay, keyframes: <literal CSS @keyframes text>}. Emit the @keyframes verbatim in a fenced css block in the Markdown so it can be copy-pasted with zero interpretation. Name the trigger explicitly (hover | press | focus | mount | in-view | state-change) — a keyframe with no trigger is unusable.

llm_needs.need: Assets shipped as real resolvable bytes with intrinsic dimensions, an explicit role, and an original-vs-rendered distinction
llm_needs.why: Figma runs a whole HTTP server for this (http://127.0.0.1:3845/assets/<sha1>.png|.svg) with three modes (placeholder / local server / download-to-project), download_assets has a raw mode returning 'the original uploaded source files … without re-rendering', and Figma's own FAQ admits the write path has 'No assets (image) support yet' with users seeing 'gray area / box instead of your images'. Builder.io's rule is blunter: 'Always explicitly define images'. EXELMJ's PlacedImage already carries naturalW/naturalH — that field is exactly right and must survive into the deliverable.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent emits , or inlines a 4MB base64 blob into a component file, or renders a vector icon as a blurry raster, or sizes an image by the design-time box and gets the aspect ratio wrong. In a fully-offline app a dangling asset reference is unrecoverable — there is no CDN to fall back to.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: ZIP: `assets/` with content-addressed filenames, plus a JSON sidecar per asset carrying {mime, naturalW, naturalH, role: photo|icon|logo|illustration|background, vector: bool, originUrl (for web-captured assets), licence/attribution if known, sha256}. Nodes reference assets by id, never by inline data. Markdown: reference by ZIP-relative path, and inline as a data: URI ONLY for small icons (state a byte ceiling, e.g. 8KB) — and add a one-line note in the manifest saying the Markdown-only delivery carries reduced asset fidelity by design. Prefer SVG source text inline for icons: it is small, diffable, recolourable, and needs no binary channel.

llm_needs.need: A cheap index up front and full detail behind it — progressive disclosure sized to a context window
llm_needs.why: Figma built an entire tool, get_metadata, for nothing but this, and the recommended flow is explicitly 'get_design_context first; if too large or truncated, get_metadata then re-fetch only the required node(s)'. The motivating real error: "MCP tool 'get_design_context' response (351378 tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)". Framelink attacks the same problem from the other side and claims ~90% compression.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: A studio with a dozen artboards produces a Markdown file no agent can read in one pass. The consumer truncates mid-structure and silently builds from a fragment, or refuses the file entirely. The ZIP fares no better if it is one monolithic JSON.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Markdown: an INDEX table in the first screen (id | name | kind: artboard/component/icon | size | states | one-line purpose), then a token section, then per-artboard and per-component sections in a fixed order, so the file degrades gracefully if truncated — a truncated heading tree is still usable, a truncated JSON object is not. ZIP: split by concern following Penpot (pages/, components/, colors/, typographies/, tokens.json, media/, objects/) plus a small `index.json`. Emit an approximate token count per section in the index so the consumer can budget.

llm_needs.need: Aggressive but reversible deduplication: a shared style table with a use-count gate, and hashed repeated node bodies
llm_needs.why: This is Framelink's finalize.ts, and the rule is worth quoting exactly: 'a style stays in globalVars only when 2+ nodes reference it (or it's a named Figma style)', single-use styles are inlined to remove pointer-chasing, named styles are kept regardless to preserve design-system intent, orphan named styles are dropped as noise; and separately 'node bodies (everything except id/name/children) that appear 2+ times are emitted once into `elements` and each occurrence is replaced by a compact { id, name, template, children? } reference', keyed by truncated SHA-1 with collision-driven lengthening.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: Either the payload is enormous (every node repeating the same twelve style properties, blowing the context budget as above), or it is over-abstracted — every colour hoisted into a table so the agent must chase three indirections to learn a button is blue, which measurably degrades output quality on small details.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Adopt the count gate verbatim: hoist a style only at 2+ references OR when it is a named/authored style; inline singletons at the node. Hash node bodies and hoist those repeating 2+ times into a `templates` table, replacing occurrences with a `template` key. Keep the string-or-object union (`fills: string | Fill[]`) so a reader never needs to know which form to expect. In Markdown, the shared tables become named sections and nodes cite them by name — the name IS the deduplication, and it reads naturally to a human.

llm_needs.need: Rendered ground-truth images per artboard, component and non-default state
llm_needs.why: Figma's get_design_context response literally instructs the agent 'you MUST call get_screenshot' afterwards, and Builder.io's critique names the lack of rendered feedback as one of three fundamental limitations of the Figma MCP: the AI has 'no visibility into the final, rendered output of its own code'.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent has no way to self-check. Structural mistakes that read fine as JSON — a flipped row/column, a z-order inversion, an overlapping absolute element, a mirrored RTL layout that should not have mirrored — pass review because there is nothing to compare against. The human reviewer also has nothing to hold the build up against.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: ZIP: `previews/<artboard-id>.png` at a stated scale, plus `previews/<component-id>.<state>.png` for each non-default state. Record width, height and devicePixelRatio next to each reference and declare the mime type correctly (Figma's server currently declares image/jpeg for PNG bytes and breaks clients — do not repeat that). Markdown: relative-path image references, and an explicit statement that a standalone Markdown delivery has no previews unless the reader also has the ZIP.

llm_needs.need: Explicit semantic role and repeat-ability per node, authored rather than inferred
llm_needs.why: Locofy's entire product mechanism is having the designer TAG layers (button, input, list, link, repeatable item) inside Figma before generation, because geometry does not carry semantics. Builder.io's import rules ask users to mark images explicitly via the Export section 'to guide the AI in identifying visual components with certainty'. Figma's MCP has no equivalent field at all — its output is a div soup with class names.
llm_needs.fails_without_it:
The agent renders a button as a styled
, so it is not focusable, not keyboard-activatable and invisible to screen readers; a list of three designed rows is hardcoded as three copies instead of a mapped array, so real data of any other length breaks the layout; an icon is emitted as an with no accessible name.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: A `role` enum per node (button | link | input | select | checkbox | list | listItem | heading | text | image | icon | container | nav | dialog | …) plus `repeats: true` with the item template id, plus `a11y: {label, labelledBy, describedBy, live}`. EXELMJ owns the authoring UI, so this is a tag the designer sets once and the format carries — it is cheap to produce and impossible for any consumer to reconstruct. In Markdown, put role in the section heading so it is unmissable.

llm_needs.need: Text direction, locale and font fallback carried as data — with measured text metrics, not bounding boxes
llm_needs.why: No format surveyed carries direction at all: Figma's inspect panel lists 'typography' and 'text strings' with no direction field; Framelink's SimplifiedNode has text/textStyle/boldWeight and nothing locale-aware; Penpot has typographies but no direction. Figma's FAQ confirms an adjacent hole — 'Fonts must be uploaded to your account to be available … Locally installed fonts that haven't been uploaded won't be accessible' — so font identity is fragile even in the incumbent. Builder.io separately warns that 'Excessive space in the bounding box can lead to issues in the output, including extra whitespace and line breaks within text layers'.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: For an Arabic-RTL-first product this is the single most expensive omission: the agent emits LTR markup with left-aligned text and left-side icons, mirrors things that must not mirror (numerals, logos, media controls, progress that tracks time), and picks a Latin fallback font that renders Arabic with broken joining and wrong line height. Nothing in the payload signals any of this is wrong, so it ships.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Per artboard and per text node: `dir: rtl|ltr|auto`, `lang`, `mirrorOnRtl: true|false` explicitly per node (not derived), `textAlign` expressed as start/end rather than left/right, and logical spacing (paddingInlineStart/End) rather than physical. Per text style: family with an ordered fallback stack, weight, size, lineHeight, letterSpacing, transform, decoration, and the numeral system. Ship the measured text metrics (rendered line count, ascent/descent, whether the box was hug or fixed) rather than the raw bounding box, so the consumer does not inherit phantom whitespace. Where fonts are licensable, embed them in the ZIP under `fonts/` with a licence sidecar; where they are not, say so in the manifest and name the fallback.

llm_needs.need: Provenance and confidence per node — especially for components captured from live websites
llm_needs.why: This is EXELMJ-specific and has NO prior art: the element picker yields markup, resolved CSS, states, motion, fonts and assets but explicitly NO per-node geometry, only the component's overall w/h. Every format surveyed assumes a single authoritative source where all geometry is known. Figma's own layer data is uniformly trustworthy; captured data is not.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: The agent treats an inferred value with the same confidence as an authored one and silently invents the missing geometry, producing a layout that is confidently wrong. Worse for a shipping product: nothing records that a component was lifted from a third-party site, so licensing and attribution obligations are invisible at the moment they matter.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: Per node: `source: authored | captured | derived`, and for captured nodes {originUrl, capturedAt, selector, userAgent/viewport at capture, and a `geometry: 'unknown'` marker with only the overall w/h populated}. Add `confidence: high|medium|low` on any inferred field. In the Markdown, captured components get a fenced note block stating the origin URL and that per-node geometry was not captured, so the consumer knows to lay out from the resolved CSS rather than from coordinates. Carry a `licence`/`attribution` field for captured assets.

llm_needs.need: A manifest declaring format version, producer version, capability flags, and unit system
llm_needs.why: Penpot's manifest.json is 'the table of contents. It tells you: Which version of the format is used [and] Which Penpot version created the file', with files also carrying format version and feature flags indicating capabilities used. Figma's Dev Mode lets the developer choose units in the Code section, which is an admission that units are ambiguous. EXELMJ's existing model positions everything in PDF POINTS from the page top-left — a unit almost no web consumer will assume.
llm_needs.fails_without_it: A consumer built against v1 silently mis-renders a v2 file instead of failing loudly. And an agent assumes CSS pixels, so every dimension in the rebuilt UI is off by a factor of 1.333 — a bug that looks like 'the design is just a bit small' and gets fixed by eyeballing rather than by reading the spec.
llm_needs.how_to_encode: manifest.json at the ZIP root and a short front-matter block at the top of the Markdown: {formatVersion, producer: 'EXELMJ x.y.z', createdAt, units: 'pt'|'px'|'dp' with an explicit conversion note, baseDpi, capabilities: ['tokens.dtcg','components.variants','motion.keyframes','capture.provenance','rtl'], counts: {artboards, components, tokens, assets}, and a 'how to read this file' section kept strictly separate from node data. Never interleave instructions with data — dev.to's teardown of Figma's MCP shows tool responses carrying directives like 'SUPER CRITICAL…' inline, which is both a prompt-injection surface and impossible to parse reliably.

summary: All fetches performed 2026-08-14. HEADLINE: the design-token question is settled — DTCG published **2025.10 as its FIRST STABLE version on 28 October 2025** ("Final Community Group Report", explicitly "considered stable", CR-equivalent), split into three modules (Format, Color, Resolver) plus a real draft-07 JSON Schema at https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/format.json that we can vendor and validate against fully offline. Anything you remember about DTCG being a perpetual draft with hex-string colours is STALE: colour is now an OBJECT ({colorSpace, components, alpha?, hex?}), dimension/duration are OBJECTS ({value, unit}), and $deprecated/$extends/$root/$ref(JSON Pointer) are all in the stable text. There is ALSO a live draft dated 30 July 2026 at designtokens.org/TR/drafts/format/ which carries a banner saying "do not implement anything in this document" — pin to 2025.10, not the draft. Caveat that matters: Style Dictionary (5.5.1, Apache-2.0) itself says "the latest format 2025.10 does not have full support yet in Style Dictionary… a work in progress in v5", so we must write 2025.10 and not assume the toolchain round-trips it. RECOMMENDATION IN ONE LINE: ADOPT DTCG 2025.10 verbatim for the token layer (it is the only thing here that is a real standard), adopt a SUBSET of the shadcn registry-item.json shape for our component/template registry (it is MIT, has an actual published schema, and its files[]/target/registryDependencies/cssVars fields map 1:1 onto what we need), BORROW the {type, content} recursive node envelope from TeleportHQ UIDL (MIT, the only real open UI intermediate representation), BORROW the manifest+directory conventions from dotLottie v2 / .penpot / .sketch for the ZIP, and IGNORE .fig (proprietary, reverse-engineered only) and .studio (InVision shut down 31 Dec 2024 — a dead format). Three gaps you must design around because no standard covers them: (1) DTCG gradient stops are ONLY {color, position} — there is no angle/linear-vs-radial, so our Shape.gradient needs an $extensions escape hatch; (2) DTCG dimension units are restricted to "px" and "rem" — our existing model is in PDF POINTS, which must be converted or explicitly declared; (3) nothing in DTCG covers per-node geometry or auto-layout, which is exactly what our website-captured components lack, so the ZIP must carry resolved CSS as the layout source of truth.

formats.name: W3C DTCG — Design Tokens Format Module
formats.license: W3C Community Group / Final Community Group Report (spec text; freely implementable, no patent encumbrance claimed)
formats.what_it_is: The interchange format for design tokens — the one genuine standard in this whole list, and the thing our colour/token system should BE rather than approximate.
formats.current_version_status: Version 2025.10. Status line seen verbatim on 2026-08-14: 'Final Community Group Report 28 October 2025', with the text 'This specification is considered stable.' It is the FIRST stable release (announced by the CG on 28 Oct 2025). Separately, a live draft at designtokens.org/TR/drafts/format/ is dated 30 July 2026 and carries a warning banner: 'This is a preview draft of in progress changes. Do not refer to this document directly, and do not implement anything in this document.' Pin to 2025.10.
formats.structure: A token is any JSON object having $value. Reserved keys: $value (required), $type, $description, $deprecated (boolean|string), $extensions (object, reverse-domain keys, MUST be preserved by tools that don't understand them). Groups are objects WITHOUT $value; groups may carry $type (inherited by descendants — precedence: token's own $type > resolved group $type after $extends > nearest ancestor group $type > invalid), plus $extends ('$extends': '{button}') to inherit from another group, and the reserved child name $root for a group's own base value. Two reference syntaxes, BOTH required: curly-brace '{group.token}' (resolves a whole $value) and $ref with RFC 6901 JSON Pointer ('#/colors/blue/$value/components/0') for sub-property access. 13 $type values: color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number, strokeStyle, border, transition, shadow, gradient, typography. CRITICAL SHAPES (verbatim from composite-types.md): dimension = {"value": 42, "unit": "px"|"rem"}; duration = {"value": 200, "unit": "ms"|"s"}; cubicBezier = [0.5,0,1,1]; fontWeight = number 1-1000 or keyword string; strokeStyle = keyword string (solid|dashed|dotted|double|groove|ridge|outset|inset) OR {"dashArray":[dimension,…],"lineCap":"round"|"butt"|"square"}; border = {"color","width","style"}; transition = {"duration","delay","timingFunction"}; shadow = object OR ARRAY of objects (layered shadows, and array entries may be aliases) with keys {"color","offsetX","offsetY","blur","spread","inset"?}; gradient = ARRAY of stops, each ONLY {"color", "position"}; typography = {"fontFamily","fontSize","fontWeight","letterSpacing","lineHeight"} where lineHeight is a bare number (1.2) not a dimension. File extension convention: '.tokens' or '.tokens.json'; MIME 'application/design-tokens+json' preferred, 'application/json' acceptable; tools SHOULD append one of those extensions on save.
formats.worth_copying: ADOPT VERBATIM. Emit tokens/*.tokens.json inside the ZIP and inline the same JSON in the Markdown. Do not invent our own token vocabulary — every downstream consumer (Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, Terrazzo, Cobalt, Penpot, Figma) reads this. THREE THINGS TO DESIGN AROUND: (a) gradient stops carry no angle and no linear/radial discriminator, so our Shape.gradient must put geometry under $extensions['app.exelmj.gradient'] = {kind:'linear'|'radial', angle, …} and keep the stop array DTCG-legal; (b) dimension units are restricted to px|rem — our existing model is in PDF POINTS, so either convert (1pt = 1.333…px) or declare the unit explicitly and never let an agent guess; (c) there is no 'opacity'/'spacing'/'radius'/'zIndex' type — those are just dimension or number, so resist adding custom $type values (a custom $type makes the file invalid; put semantics in the group path instead, e.g. spacing.md).

formats.name: W3C DTCG — Color Module
formats.license: W3C Community Group / Final Community Group Report
formats.what_it_is: The separately-versioned module that defines what a color token's $value actually looks like. This is the single biggest breaking change from every pre-2025 DTCG example you will find online.
formats.current_version_status: Version 2025.10, 'Final Community Group Report, 28 October 2025'. Verified 2026-08-14.
formats.structure: color $value is an OBJECT, never a hex string: {"colorSpace": <string, required>, "components": <array of numbers or the keyword "none", required>, "alpha": <number 0–1, optional, defaults to 1>, "hex": <optional 6-digit CSS hex fallback — MUST be 6 digits, no alpha, to avoid conflicting with the alpha field>}. 14 allowed colorSpace values: srgb, srgb-linear, hsl, hwb, lab, lch, oklab, oklch, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, xyz-d65, xyz-d50. Example seen verbatim: {"colorSpace":"srgb","components":[0,0.4,0.8],"hex":"#0066cc"}. Note components for srgb are 0–1 floats, NOT 0–255.
formats.worth_copying: ADOPT VERBATIM, and always write the optional "hex" fallback. Rationale specific to us: the element picker captures resolved CSS from live sites, which today is overwhelmingly srgb hex/rgb() but increasingly oklch() (shadcn's own registry now ships oklch cssVars). Storing {colorSpace:'oklch', components:[…], hex:'#…'} preserves the site's real gamut while still giving a downstream agent a hex it can paste. Write a tiny offline converter (srgb<->oklch) in vanilla TS — no dependency needed, the math is ~40 lines.

formats.name: W3C DTCG — Resolver Module
formats.license: W3C Community Group / Final Community Group Report
formats.what_it_is: The standard answer to 'how do I ship light/dark, LTR/RTL, brand-A/brand-B, and density variants without duplicating every token file'. Most teams don't know this exists.
formats.current_version_status: Version 2025.10, 'Final Community Group Report, 28 October 2025'. Verified 2026-08-14.
formats.structure: A resolver document declares: sets — collections of DTCG tokens, each with a sources array that may reference external .tokens.json files OR inline token objects; modifiers — each with a REQUIRED contexts map (key -> array of token sources), and an optional default that MUST match one of the context keys; resolutionOrder — an array naming sets and modifiers, where LATER entries override earlier ones on conflict. A consumer supplies an input object naming each modifier and the chosen context, and the resolver produces one flat permutation. Recommended file extension '.resolver.json', MIME 'application/json'.
formats.worth_copying: ADOPT A SUBSET — specifically sets + modifiers.contexts + resolutionOrder, and skip nothing else because there isn't much else. This is a direct fit for EXELMJ: modifiers named 'theme' (contexts light/dark), 'direction' (contexts rtl/ltr — our Arabic-first requirement becomes a first-class token axis rather than a hack), and 'density'. Ship exactly one tokens/design.resolver.json in the ZIP. In the single-Markdown delivery, ALSO ship the pre-resolved permutation for the default context inline, because a Markdown reader cannot execute a resolver — give the agent the answer, not the recipe.

formats.name: DTCG JSON Schema (format.json)
formats.license: Published alongside the CG report
formats.what_it_is: A real, machine-readable draft-07 JSON Schema for the stable format — meaning we can validate our export offline with a ~10KB vendored file and zero runtime dependency.
formats.current_version_status: Live and fetched successfully 2026-08-14. $id: https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/format.json, $schema: http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#, title: 'DTCG Format Schema'. The spec's own examples reference it via a "$schema" key at the top of token files.
formats.structure: Discriminates token-vs-group purely by presence of $value. $type is an enum of the 13 names. $type/$description/$extensions/$extends/$deprecated are permitted on both tokens and groups.
formats.worth_copying: ADOPT VERBATIM — vendor this file into the repo (it is draft-07, so a small hand-rolled validator or a permissive-licensed one like ajv (MIT) works fully offline) and run it in a unit test on every export. Also emit "$schema": "https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/format.json" as the first key of each .tokens.json we write; it costs one line and instantly tells any consuming agent which spec revision it is holding. This is the cheapest correctness win in the whole shard.

formats.name: Style Dictionary
formats.license: Apache-2.0
formats.what_it_is: The de-facto build system that turns .tokens.json into CSS/JS/Swift/Dart/Kotlin. Relevant to us not as a dependency but as the consumer whose expectations our export must satisfy.
formats.current_version_status: v5.5.1 on npm as of 2026-08-14 (license Apache-2.0, engines.node >=22.0.0, ESM-only exports './lib/StyleDictionary.js'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT read verbatim from styledictionary.com/info/dtcg/ on 2026-08-14: first-class DTCG support exists 'since version 4', BUT 'the latest format 2025.10 does not have full support yet in Style Dictionary' and this is 'a work in progress in v5'. So v5 is current but its 2025.10 coverage is incomplete.
formats.structure: Config top level: source (string[] globs), include (string[] globs, overridden by source), tokens (inline object), platforms (Record<string,Platform>), log, hooks (custom preprocessors/parsers/transforms/formats), preprocessors (string[]), expand (ExpandConfig, for exploding composite tokens), usesDtcg (boolean — the flag that switches it into $value/$type mode). Platform: transformGroup, transforms (string[]), buildPath (trailing slash REQUIRED), prefix, files (File[]), actions (string[]). File: destination, format, filter (string|fn|object), options {showFileHeader, fileHeader, outputReferences}. Predefined formats that matter to us, exact names: css/variables, json, json/flat, json/nested, json/asset, javascript/es6, javascript/esm, javascript/module, typescript/es6-declarations, typescript/module-declarations, scss/variables, scss/map-deep, less/variables. Flutter and Compose DO exist: flutter/class.dart and compose/object. Also android/resources, android/colors, android/dimens, ios-swift/class.swift, ios-swift/enum.swift, and sketch/palette + sketch/palette/v2.
formats.worth_copying: BORROW IDEAS, DO NOT DEPEND. Do not bundle Style Dictionary into an Electron app (ESM-only, node>=22, and its 2025.10 support is admittedly incomplete). Instead: (1) make our .tokens.json files valid input for `usesDtcg: true` so a user CAN run SD over them, and (2) optionally ship a ready-made config.json in the ZIP root (tokens/style-dictionary.config.json) with usesDtcg:true and platforms for css/variables + json/nested — this turns our bundle into something a developer can build from in one command without us shipping a single byte of SD. The predefined-format names above are also the right vocabulary for our own tiny built-in exporters: name our CSS emitter 'css/variables' so it is instantly legible. Answer to the Flutter/Compose question: yes, flutter/class.dart and compose/object are built in, so we do NOT need to invent mobile output — we just need to be valid SD input.

formats.name: Tokens Studio JSON (+ @tokens-studio/sd-transforms)
formats.license: sd-transforms is MIT (v2.0.3, peerDependency style-dictionary ^5.0.0). The Figma plugin itself is a commercial product.
formats.what_it_is: The most widely used real-world token file format in the wild — the format most designers' token JSON is actually in. Matters to us as an IMPORT source, not an export target.
formats.current_version_status: Verified 2026-08-14 on both docs.tokens.studio and the raw GitHub docs source: Tokens Studio still supports TWO formats — 'legacy' and 'W3C DTCG' — and the docs state plainly 'The default is legacy format.' It is NOT yet DTCG-by-default. The docs also concede alignment gaps: 'The DTCG specifies additional token types and their accepted values, which we will support in future releases.' @tokens-studio/sd-transforms is at 2.0.3, MIT.
formats.structure: Legacy: unprefixed keys value / type / description. DTCG mode: the same content re-keyed to $value / $type / $description; the plugin converts the whole file set on switch (and, if synced to git, opens a branch with a pre-filled commit). Tokens Studio carries extra type names that are NOT DTCG $type values: boxShadow, composition, sizing, spacing, borderRadius, opacity, typography, asset. Its values are also frequently strings with units baked in ('16px', '#fff', '1.5') rather than DTCG's {value,unit} objects and colour objects, and it supports math expressions in values.
formats.worth_copying: BORROW IDEAS ONLY — do not adopt Tokens Studio JSON as our format. Concretely: write a one-way IMPORTER (Tokens Studio -> DTCG 2025.10) so a designer can drop their existing token file into EXELMJ. The mapping is mechanical and worth writing down: value->$value, type->$type, description->$description; sizing|spacing|borderRadius -> $type 'dimension' with the unit parsed out of the string into {value,unit}; opacity -> 'number'; boxShadow -> 'shadow'; composition -> DROP into $extensions (no DTCG equivalent); asset -> DROP into $extensions. The real lesson to steal is their $extensions discipline: everything proprietary goes in a reverse-domain namespace so the file stays spec-valid. We should use exactly one namespace, 'app.exelmj', for artboard geometry, capture provenance, gradient angle, and RTL metadata.

formats.name: shadcn/ui registry — registry-item.json
formats.license: MIT (shadcn-ui/ui, Copyright (c) 2023 shadcn)
formats.what_it_is: A published JSON Schema for describing a distributable UI component: its files, its npm deps, its cross-registry deps, and the CSS variables it needs. This is the single best model for our component/template registry and it is MIT.
formats.current_version_status: Schema fetched live 2026-08-14 and is current. Note one deprecation seen in the docs: the `tailwind` object is DEPRECATED, superseded by `cssVars.theme` for Tailwind v4 — do not copy `tailwind`.
formats.structure: REAL top-level field names, verbatim from the schema: $schema, name, type, title, description, author, dependencies, devDependencies, registryDependencies, files, tailwind (deprecated), cssVars, css, envVars, meta, docs, categories, extends, style, iconLibrary, baseColor, theme, font. `type` enum (12 values): registry:lib, registry:block, registry:component, registry:ui, registry:hook, registry:theme, registry:page, registry:file, registry:style, registry:base, registry:font, registry:item. files[] = {path (required, relative to registry root), content (string, the actual file body — this is how a registry ships self-contained), type (required, mirrors the type enum), target (conditionally required — mandatory for registry:file and registry:page; supports the placeholders @components/, @ui/, @lib/, @hooks/ and ~/ for project root)}. cssVars = {theme, light, dark} each a flat map of custom-property name -> value (values are now oklch(...) strings). css = a nested object mirroring at-rules/layers/utilities (@layer, @keyframes, @plugin, @utility). registryDependencies = string[] resolved five ways: bare name ('button'), namespaced ('@acme/input-form'), GitHub ('owner/repo/item#tag'), absolute URL ('https://example.com/r/item.json'), or local ('./item.json'). meta = unconstrained key/value. envVars = flat string map. docs = a markdown/instruction string. categories = string[]. SEPARATE ROOT SCHEMA at https://ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry.json: {$schema, name, homepage, include, items, pagination} — requires items OR include (anyOf); items[] each $ref the registry-item schema; pagination = {total, offset, limit, hasMore}. There is NO `extends` on the root schema.
formats.worth_copying: ADOPT A SUBSET — this is my strongest recommendation after DTCG. Take, verbatim in spirit and in field name: name, type, title, description, author, files[] {path, content, target}, registryDependencies, dependencies, cssVars, docs, categories, meta. Swap the `type` enum for our own vocabulary (exelmj:component, exelmj:template, exelmj:artboard, exelmj:icon, exelmj:token-set, exelmj:capture) but KEEP the '<namespace>:<kind>' string shape and keep the rule that files[].type mirrors it. FOUR SPECIFIC IDEAS WORTH STEALING: (1) files[].content inlines the file body — that is exactly how one item becomes self-describing, and it is precisely what makes the single-Markdown delivery possible at all; (2) `target` with @-placeholders separates 'where it lives in my bundle' from 'where it should land in your project', which is the whole handoff problem in one field; (3) registryDependencies-by-URL-or-local-path gives us component composition across bundles for free; (4) the two-schema split (root registry.json listing items + one registry-item.json per item) is exactly the ZIP-root-manifest + per-component-file layout we need. AVOID: `tailwind` (deprecated), and don't copy `style`/`baseColor`/`iconLibrary` — they are shadcn-CLI-specific.

formats.name: Custom Elements Manifest (custom-elements.json)
formats.license: BSD-3-Clause (npm package `custom-elements-manifest`)
formats.what_it_is: The standard machine-readable description of a web component's PUBLIC API — attributes, events, slots, CSS parts, CSS custom properties, CSS states. The best available vocabulary for 'what knobs does this component expose'.
formats.current_version_status: npm package `custom-elements-manifest` at 2.1.0, BSD-3-Clause, description 'A file format for describing custom elements'. Verified 2026-08-14. The schema itself is JSON Schema draft-07. schemaVersion is a free-form string field in Package that tracks the schema's own semver (currently 2.1.0) — it is not hard-coded as a const in the schema.
formats.structure: Package (root, required): {schemaVersion: string, modules: JavaScriptModule[], readme?: string, deprecated?: boolean|string}. JavaScriptModule: {kind: 'javascript-module', path: string, summary?, description?, declarations?: Declaration[], exports?: Export[], deprecated?}. Declaration kinds: 'class' | 'function' | 'mixin' | 'variable' | 'custom-element'. Export kinds: 'js' | 'custom-element-definition'. CustomElementDeclaration extends ClassDeclaration and adds: customElement (required, must be true), tagName?, attributes: Attribute[], events: Event[], slots: Slot[], cssParts: CssPart[], cssProperties: CssCustomProperty[], cssStates: CssCustomState[], demos: Demo[]. Inherited from ClassDeclaration: kind:'class', name (required), members: (ClassField|ClassMethod)[], superclass: Reference, mixins: Reference[], description, summary, deprecated, source. Attribute: {name, summary?, description?, type?, default?, fieldName? (the property it reflects to), deprecated?}. ClassField: {kind:'field', name, type?, static?, privacy?, readonly?}. Reference: {name, package?, module?} — a portable cross-package pointer.
formats.worth_copying: BORROW IDEAS — adopt the VOCABULARY, not the file. We are vanilla TS and not shipping custom elements, so a literal custom-elements.json would be a lie. But CEM's five-axis breakdown of a component's surface — attributes / slots / events / cssProperties / cssParts / cssStates — is the most complete and battle-tested checklist in existence for 'what must I document so someone can re-use this'. Map it onto our captured components: attributes -> the props/variants we infer; slots -> the content holes in the captured markup; events -> nothing (drop it); cssProperties -> the DTCG token aliases the component consumes (this is the join between our token layer and our component layer); cssStates -> the :hover/:focus-visible/:active/:disabled states the element picker captured. Also steal Reference {name, package, module} as the shape for every cross-item pointer in our bundle, and steal the mandatory top-level schemaVersion string — our manifest must declare its own version, and CEM shows the minimum viable way.

formats.name: Storybook CSF (Component Story Format) + argTypes
formats.license: MIT (storybook 10.5.8)
formats.what_it_is: The most widely-adopted informal description of a component's props and their editable controls. argTypes is effectively a UI-control schema, which is more useful to us than CSF itself.
formats.current_version_status: storybook npm package at 10.5.8, MIT, verified 2026-08-14. CSF 3 is the current recommended standard. CSF Factories ('CSF Next') exists — definePreview, defineMain, preview.meta({...}), meta.story({...}), plus a defineMeta helper — and Storybook 10 promotes it, though it began as an experimental Storybook 8 feature and framework coverage rolled out React-first with Vue/Angular/Web Components landing across 10.x. Storybook explicitly states CSF 1, 2 and 3 remain supported and none are deprecated. NOTE: stories.json was REMOVED in Storybook 8; the machine-readable index is now served at the /index.json route and is produced by the Indexers API — so there is no longer a stable 'docs JSON' artifact to target.
formats.structure: Story file = a default export (meta) + named exports (stories). meta: {component (required in CSF factories), title?, decorators?, parameters?, args?, argTypes?, tags?, includeStories?, excludeStories?}. Story object: {name?, args, argTypes?, parameters?, decorators?, render?, play?}. argTypes is a map argName -> {name?, description?, type (scalar 'boolean'|'string'|'number'|'function'|'symbol', or complex array/object/enum/union/intersection; may be {name, required}), control (a string type, or {type, min, max, step, presetColors, accept, labels}, or false to disable), options (array of the finite legal values), mapping (option string -> complex value), if (conditional display keyed on another arg or a global), table {category, subcategory, defaultValue {summary, detail}, type {summary, detail}, disable, readonly}}. defaultValue on argTypes is DEPRECATED — put defaults in meta.args instead.
formats.worth_copying: BORROW IDEAS, adopt argTypes as a SUBSET. Do NOT emit .stories.ts files — that would bind our offline vanilla-TS app to a React/Vite/Storybook toolchain we don't have, and CSF Factories is still churning. DO steal the argTypes object as the schema for a component's variant/prop surface, because it uniquely encodes three things nothing else here does: the ENUMERATION of legal values (options), the CONTROL AFFORDANCE (control.type — which is literally what our studio's inspector panel needs to render), and the DEFAULT (via meta.args). One field is worth copying outright: `table.category` — it is how you group 20 props into 'Appearance / Behaviour / Accessibility' in generated docs, and our Markdown delivery needs exactly that grouping. Also note for the parent agent: since stories.json is gone as of Storybook 8, 'Storybook docs JSON' is no longer a real interop target — argTypes-as-a-shape is the only durable thing to take.
